The 8 Best Outdoor Security Cameras Keep an Eye on Your Home When You're Away

📅 29 Mar 2021 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • It has been revealed that keeping your home safe these days takes more than a deadbolt and a dog with a menacing bark.
  • Outdoor security cameras in particular are your best bet to prevent break-ins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that keeping your home safe these days takes more than a deadbolt and a dog with a menacing bark. Installing a few security cameras around your property is an easy and surprisingly cost-effective way to level up your home security, adding watchful eyes that track comings and goings 24/7. Until relatively recently, the only options for personal home security were comprehensive (and expensive) systems that were installed and monitored by security professionals. Now, you can set up your own cameras and home security system that saves you cash without sacrificing performance.

Outdoor security cameras in particular are your best bet to prevent break-ins. According to Security.org, simply having a clearly visible camera or security device on your property serves as a strong deterrent for trespassers. Outdoor security cameras are equipped with features found in indoor security cameras like high-definition video, night vision, two-way audio, and more. In addition to this, they come equipped with outdoor-specific features like weather-resistant exteriors, sound detection, and integrated motion-activated spotlights.

For this guide, we got our hands on the most promising options from well-established brands including Arlo, Wyze, Ring, and Eufy and tested them at our homes and offices. Read on below to learn about the best outdoor security cameras we recommend, along with expert advice to help you choose the right option for your home and budget.

One quick note before we dive in: It’s increasingly notable to pick security gear that’s compatible with whatever smart home system you already have. For example, Amazon makes it easy to pull up a live feed from your Ring camera(s) on an Echo Show or Fire TV and has designed its products to more seamlessly connect with its other smart home devices. Same goes for Google products. If you already have a few items from a major smart home brand, consider buying gear that will be as compatible as possible with it.

More Home Improvement Stories: Best Retractable Awnings ● The Popular Mechanics 2025 Yard & Garden Awards ● Best Solar-Powered Outdoor Lights.

In a recent development, we selected our recommendations based on a round of substantial testing: We installed these cameras outdoors, and used them to survey our homes for weeks, and in some cases months. We watched them as they watched our properties, as they endured a wide spectrum of outdoor conditions including snow and rain.

We tested and compared their basic video recording functionality, evaluating them on clarity, field of view, and weather resistance as well as any special features they offer like spotlights, solar charging, sirens, and more. Some of the cameras on this list were tested in outdoor settings for months, facing a wide spectrum of outdoor conditions including snow and rain.

We also tested their more nuanced security and tech features, including motion detection notifications, AI recognition of animals and packages, two-way audio conversations, and digital borders, among others. These features were considered as well as the cost, if any, associated with buying access to all of them.

We recommended the Wyze Outdoor Cam V2 ahead of testing, based on its low price, solid specs, and the past performance of other Wyze cameras that we've tested.

According to recent reports, the Arlo Essential XL stands out for its user-friendly design, durable exterior, and of course, its clear video quality—all for a fair price. It's completely wireless, which means you can mount it anywhere around your home without worrying about power and wiring issues.

Industry observers note that it excels as a 24/7 outdoor cam, with features like color night vision that improves the clarity of nighttime footage. During testing, we were impressed by its resolution in low light, as well as its accurate motion detection. It provides real-time alerts directly to your smartphone, and will let you check a live feed to observe any suspicious activity live as it happens.

You can also program the integrated spotlight to automatically flash on when someone is within visual range. It's a great deterrent against potential robberies, and lets you leave the house without leaving a porch light on.

While this cam has solid features without a subscription, an Arlo Secure subscription adds cloud storage for your video footage, as well as additional target recognition and home security features, for $96 to $300 per year.

Arlo Essential XL Security Camera Review.

Few options balance price and quality as well as this affordable option from Wyze. The battery-operated Wyze Outdoor V2 camera can be mounted anywhere. New buyers should pick up the starter kit, which includes a base unit that allows you to expand your system with up to four cameras.

Though it's the most affordable on the list, it still offers a lineup of powerful features including motion-sensing technology that detects both body heat and movement, reducing the number of potential false alarms drastically.

The Wyze is also quite flexible for storage options with the camera capable of online cloud storage as well as localized storage on a microSD card.

Solar-powered cameras, while power-efficient, present extra setup challenges. Most of the time, the panel is attached to the body of the camera, so you need to need find to camera positions with a good field of view and get good sun exposure. Depending on the layout of your home and the surrounding area, that may lead to less-than-ideal placements, which create holes in your surveillance.

The Tapo MagCam solves this concern with a detachable solar panel, so you can keep it connected when it's effective, or remove and mount it higher above the camera to get more sun. It features a 13-foot extension cord, so you have a good amount of slack to move it to an open, sunshiny space.

Test Editor Bradley Ford mounted his test camera in a semi-shaded area, then set up the solar panel in direct sunlight. Despite the fact that he was testing at the end of 2025, when there was significantly less daily sunlight, the battery never dipped below 80 percent charge. In the warmer weather, the camera typically sat at 100 percent.

Sources indicate that in addition, Ford preferred that the MagCam relied on local storage. "One of the things we like best is that there is no need for a subscription to access activation videos," Ford stated. "They’re all stored locally on a Micro SD card in the camera. However, if you wish to pay for cloud storage, that option is also available.".

This specific kit comes with a camera, solar panel, and mount, however Tapo offers others with two or three cameras as well.

Sources indicate that our previous pick in this category, the Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Plus, was a terrific outdoor security camera that featured a dual-LED floodlight. The latest Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro builds on that solid design with extra features, including support for dual-band WiFi and a “bird’s-eye view” feature that tracks a recorded subject as they move within the camera’s view, showing it on a top-down layout of the area.

The camera’s 1080p video resolution and 140-degree field of view are the same as the previous model, but image quality is enhanced with high dynamic range (HDR) support, which improves visibility in both low light and extremely bright conditions.

The lights themselves are also quite bright, 2000 lumens each, and the fixtures are adjustable so you can angle the light as you please.

The Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro also features two-way audio support, with a 110-decibel siren that sounds when the system detects motion. It also offers customizable motion zones and 3D- motion radar for you to tailor to your property.

A word of warning: We found the wired installation was fairly difficult, so we recommend hiring an electrician unless you're experienced with wiring and up for a challenge.

Industry observers note that unlike any other outdoor security camera on our list, this option from Tactacam does not require a WiFi connection. Instead, it connects to cellular towers and works similarly to your smartphone. This makes the camera perfect for homes in remote locations.

The security camera does require a monthly subscription for access to on-demand videos and photos that are stored in the cloud, but aims start at just 5 bucks a month.

The device works with AA batteries or a rechargeable battery pack. In our testing, we took anywhere from two to 10 pictures a day and the pack lasted about three to four months before needing to be recharged.

In practice, the security camera is great at sensing motion more than 100 feet away, so it could potentially double as a nature cam. It lacks some of the features other, similarly priced models on this list have, but the biggest drawback is that the field of view is only about 50 feet wide.

The Arlo floodlight has everything we love from our top pick, including Arlo's superior app and software, but adds on a large floodlight, as well as a need for wired power.

As with the Arlo Essential XL, you get quality motion detection software and color night vision. Spring for Arlo Secure, and you get AI target recognition that can point out passing cars or faces, and highlight packages.

In a recent development, the floodlight also has some interesting features: Each light is individually adjustable, so you can angle them for the best possible coverage. That includes creative solutions like angling one light toward your back door, while pointing the other toward the steps leading to your back porch. It's a small touch, but a very appreciated one. It also includes a loud, 110-decibel siren.

If you're looking for a low-maintenance outdoor security camera system, eufy's S330 "eufycam 3" is a dynamic wireless option that supports solar charging and doesn't require professional installation.

Once installed and set up, we did not have to take either of the cameras down for recharging once over months of use. The solar panels kept them perpetually charged as long as they got exposure to a few hours of sunlight per day.

It was similarly easy to connect the cameras to the greater home security. The outdoor cameras works through the home hub which after initial installation using an ethernet cable, works comfortably through your home WiFi. The cameras can then be set up anywhere within several hundred feet of the hub without losing connection.

A big benefit we also loved is the camera system requires no monthly subscription to access its features. This includes AI-powered face recognition, customizable activity zones, and of course, motion detection.

In a recent development, the only drawback for this camera set is the placement of the solar panels. While the panels being integrated directly on top of the camera makes it less cumbersome, it also means you need to install them in a spot with direct sunlight or they won't properly charge.

In a recent development, the Reolink Argus 4 Pro gives you a sweeping 180-degree field of view, which allows you to cover large open spaces with as few cameras as possible. Properly positioned, you can achieve a near-complete view of an area with just two cameras.

According to recent reports, this 4K camera features a dual-lens design that covers larger areas without blind spots or fishbowl-style warping. You'd think that might lead to complications with position or usage, but we found it easy to operate.

It features discrete solar panels for power, which allows for more placement flexibility: For example, you can install the camera under a ledge or rooftop, then secure the solar panel above, where it will get direct sun. That makes it easier to get the perfect shot and optimal power.

It has been revealed that in terms of storage, the Argus 4 Pro records footage locally and connects to a home hub. You don't have to pay a monthly fee for cloud storage or additional features. Simply turn it on, connect it the hub, and in theory, it should run without issue in perpetuity.

There are two types of consumer-grade home security cameras: wireless battery-powered cameras that you can set up easily nearly anywhere, but require you to occasionally replace batteries, and wired models that connect directly to your home's electrical system.

It has been revealed that wired cameras are generally more expensive and require an electrician's help unless you're comfortable with home wiring, but require far less maintenance once they're installed. Their placement is also restricted to locations where you can wired them in.

Battery-powered cameras, by contrast, are only restricted by the range of your WiFi router. Of course, you'll need to access them every few months to replace their batteries. Some models feature solar panels, giving you renewable energy, but panels also impose some placement restrictions. (Namely, access to sunlight).

Wired cameras do fall short of battery-powered models in one niche scenario—when the power goes out. Unlike, say, wired smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, which have reliable battery backup, you can't count on a wired security camera to provide surveillance footage during an extended period of time if there's a power failure. It varies from model to model, but most wired cameras can only last for 30 minutes to, at most, a few hours before they go dark.

According to recent reports, to avoid recording 24/7, which wastes power and storage space, outdoor security cameras usually feature motion sensors that trigger recording whenever there’s activity. Many cameras will also an alert to your companion app whenever they start recording.

It has been revealed that most cameras give you the ability to calibrate the motion sensor by setting motion zones in spots where you expect frequent false alarms, like a sidewalk. Others offer smart features that can differentiate between people, animals, and vehicles. You should also have the ability to customize your notifications, so you’ll only receive an alert in certain situations, like if it detects a person.

Furthermore, some cameras feature microphones, enabling audio detection, which can trigger recording and alerts based on nearby sounds that may be out of view (like a window breaking). Audio detection is a useful extra layer in a few specific situations, like when a single camera can’t cover the entire side of your home, but may also lead to more nuisance alerts. If you decide to use one, we recommend customizing your audio alert sensitivity if possible so you aren’t constantly getting notified when the neighbor’s dog barks.

According to recent reports, the best outdoor security cameras record video in "Full HD" (1920 x 1080p) resolution, which captures enough detail to identify facial features or a car’s license plate. More expensive cameras record at higher resolutions, such as 2K or "Quad HD" (2560 x 1440p) or 4K Ultra HD (3840 x 2160) video, which deliver better detail. While higher resolution may help, 1080p video is usually clear enough to give you more than enough information in most situations.

Your camera’s field of view (FOV) is just as important as its resolution. Field of view refers to how wide of an angle the lens is and therefore, how much of your yard or porch is in view. With a wider FOV, your camera can see a wider area around your property, providing more coverage. For the best results, we recommend a model with a field of view between 130 and 180 degrees.

Many outdoor cameras also feature an integrated spotlight that can illuminate the surroundings if motion is detected, improving visibility in low-light situations. A spotlight also acts as a deterrent by making potential intruders more visible. Similarly, the majority of outdoor cameras offer some kind of night vision feature, which uses infrared (IR) lights to record a high-contrast black and white video in the dark. Top-of-the-line cameras are capable of recording standard video in low light, minimizing the need for night vision.

It has been revealed that there’s no point in recording camera footage if you can’t store it for when you need it. Many manufacturers offer free cloud storage for a limited time—typically seven days–after which video is overwritten with new recordings. You can always download and save that footage, so long as you do during that initial window.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to save your footage for a longer period, there are a couple of options. Many companies provide additional cloud storage for a subscription fee. There are also cameras that feature a microSD card slot for storing footage locally. This does require a bit of extra maintenance in the form of occasionally removing the card and either deleting or downloading the recorded data to free up more space on the card.

If you’re concerned with privacy, be aware that cloud footage is generally kept on a manufacturer’s servers, which can be stolen if the company’s digital security is breached. Some companies may also use or share data from stored recordings in ways you might not anticipate. For example, Amazon has shared footage from Ring cameras to law enforcement without customers’ permission on many occasions. While storing locally requires more legwork, it is definitely the most secure option for privacy-conscious homeowners.

Security cameras are more than just their features. Nearly all security cameras are built to connect with other smart home devices. So, before buying any specific option, make sure it is compatible with the devices you already own. For example, Amazon makes it easy to pull up a live feed from your Ring camera(s) on an Echo Show or Fire TV. There are many brands that work with the majority of the smart home software available such as Apple, Google Nest, and Ring. Some have limited functionality on other smart home software systems outside of their brand, but still work with them. Furthermore, most security camera brands require a monthly subscription to gain full access to many of their features. These monthly subscriptions range in price and overall necessity with some basically essential to operate the cameras and store footage in the cloud while others are designed as a bonus add-on to the base product. Prior to purchase, make sure to take a close look at both the smart home compatibility as well as what comes with and without the monthly subscription service.

Most of the outdoor security cameras we recommend are sold individually or as part of a larger set. The number of cameras you need for your property will vary, based on your home security plan and how much camera coverage you want. A well-installed camera with a wide field of view can cover an crucial and vulnerable area on your property, such as a back door or garage.

That remarked, even a small home will need at least a few cameras to achieve full coverage on every ground-level door and window. You may need multiple cameras to reveal tricky blind spots created by corners, lawn features, and anything else that might impede a single camera position.

Industry observers note that don't freak out about needing a fleet of surveillance gear, though. Not everyone wants or needs to have every single square inch of their property under constant watch. It’s up to you to decide where you want an extra eye. The vital thing is to make sure you know what you need before making a purchase.

Of course. There are no features of an outdoor security camera that would prevent it from working inside. That said, many companies make indoor cameras that are cheaper, and may feature a stand or mounting options that make more sense for blending in with your home or office.

Recent findings suggest that you should always be careful when considering home security. Over the years, there have been multiple reports of strangers accessing live video feeds and recorded videos from home security cameras.

Luckily, there are simple ways to protect yourself. As with other devices, adhering to digital security best practices, such as keeping your smart home devices’ firmware up to date, creating a strong password and activating two-factor authentication wherever possible, will help prevent a breach.

You may also have concerns about who has access to video that’s stored in the cloud. Most companies ask for permission to review recordings for research and development purposes. Depending on the company, this request often comes in the form of an “opt-in” setting in the camera app, though some may turn it on by default unless you “opt out.”.

Recent findings suggest that some may also share recordings with law enforcement. In some cases, they will only do so when compelled by a search warrant. A couple manufacturers, specifically Amazon (Ring) and Google (Nest), have said they will provide footage without a warrant if law enforcement claims it is an emergency.

Industry News: Charred Cabbage With Yogurt and Hot Sauce

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you think cabbage is boring, this dish will absolutely change your mind.
  • According to recent reports, in a blender, combine 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp.
  • Preheat the oven to 425°F and set racks in the center and top of the oven.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you think cabbage is boring, this dish will absolutely change your mind. Charred aggressively, it takes on a smoky, almost meaty quality—it’s the main event. A drizzle of hot sauce, crispy breadcrumbs, and a cooling yogurt sauce round it out. Treat cabbage like a protein, and it will reward you.

More showstopping cabbage recipes here.

According to recent reports, in a blender, combine 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp. brine, 1 small shallot, roughly chopped, 3 garlic cloves, 3 Tbsp. red wine vinegar, juice of 1 navel orange, and 1 tsp. kosher salt. Blend on high, taking a pause to scrape the sides, until smooth. With the blender running on low, slowly pour in 1 cup extra-virgin olive oil until the sauce is silky and runny. Transfer the sauce to a bottle or jar and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

Preheat the oven to 425°F and set racks in the center and top of the oven. Line a sheet tray with parchment paper.

It has been revealed that make the Cabbage: Cut 1 large head green cabbage in half, then slice each half into four wedges. Arrange on the prepared sheet tray, drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil and kosher salt, and massage it into all those craggy layers. Roast on the center rack for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides through easily. Set the broiler to high and slide the cabbage to the top rack. Broil for 2–4 minutes, until the edges are deeply charred and irresistibly crispy.

While the Cabbage Roasts, Make the Breadcrumbs: In a small skillet over medium heat, melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter with 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Stir in ½ cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 garlic clove, finely grated, and ½ tsp. kosher salt, then toast, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant. Remove from the heat and mix in ¼ preserved lemon, store-bought or homemade, peel only, finely diced, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, and 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley. Set aside to cool.

Sources indicate that make the Yogurt: In a small bowl, whisk together 1 cup full-fat Greek yogurt or labne, zest and juice ½ lemon, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley, and 1 tsp. kosher salt until smooth and creamy.

When the cabbage is ready, swoop the yogurt across a serving plate. Arrange the cabbage wedges at dramatic angles. Drizzle generously with hot sauce, letting it seep into the leaves. Finish with the golden breadcrumbs, fresh dill fronds, and a few extra grates of lemon zest. Serve immediately.

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (424 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

  • Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

According to recent reports, whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

It has been revealed that arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

According to recent reports, combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a significant pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Between the salmon sperm facials, the skin boosters, and the next generation of lasers, there’s plenty to pique the interest of the beauty obsessive in South Korea. So much so that vacations are increasingly being organized around visits to the dermatologist’s office. But how much is too much when it comes to our beauty itineraries? Just ask Khloé and Kim Kardashian.

On Wednesday’s episode of her podcast, Khloé in Wonder Land, Koko and her close friend La La Anthony reminisced about their August 2025 trip to South Korea, where they enthusiastically availed themselves of the country’s advanced cosmetic treatments—with some less-than-desirable results.

“Kim and I came back deformed, you came back beautiful and the plane ride just made it so much worse,” Kardashian told Anthony, recalling how their post-treatment appearances had kept them holed up in their hotel room.

Industry observers note that the Kardashians are, of course, well-versed in the world of aesthetics. Over the years, the sisters have been particularly candid about their experiments with everything from the vampire facial to regenerative skin treatments. But even for those with the world’s most sought-after dermatologists on speed dial, things don’t always go to plan.

Recent findings suggest that while it’s unclear precisely which procedures the sisters underwent—photos shared on Kim’s Instagram at the time demonstrated her receiving facial treatments and an IV infusion—their experience raises some pertinent questions. How much research should we be doing before traveling abroad for cosmetic treatments? How many procedures can we feasibly—and safely—fit into a vacation? And how do we know when something has actually gone wrong?

In a recent development, the lure of a beauty vacation is understandable. South Korea, in particular, is at the forefront of aesthetic innovation, with technologies and treatments that aren’t yet widely available in the United States. And as our collective beauty literacy has expanded, so too has our appetite for more technologically sophisticated treatments. A facial no longer necessarily means an hour of extractions and massage. But there is a distinction to be made between a beauty treatment and a medical procedure. Just because something is marketed as minimally invasive, or requires no incisions, doesn’t mean it is without risk. Nor does its ubiquity on TikTok necessarily speak to its suitability for your own skin.

“Traveling for treatment isn't the same as having unsafe treatment,” says consultant dermatologist Dr. Sidra Khan. “What travel adds is complexity: a different regulatory system, possibly a language barrier, often a compressed consultation, and being thousands of miles from your practitioner during recovery.”.

It has been revealed that “A beautiful clinic, an impressive Instagram following and a gallery of celebrity clients don’t really tell you much about the practitioner’s medical credentials or what results you might expect,” adds cosmetic surgeon and aesthetics specialist Dr. Paul Banwell. Independently verify your practitioner’s qualifications and registration with the relevant medical regulator, and establish whether the clinic is equipped to manage complications. Khan recommends arranging a virtual consultation with the treating doctor before booking anything, and asking about their experience with your particular skin tone, the products and devices they intend to use, and why. “A holiday itinerary shouldn't replace informed consent.”.

Sources indicate that for London-based aesthetics and NHS doctor Dr. Alicia Gonzalez-Fernandez, the marketing of medical procedures as vacation packages is itself a red flag. “On a handful of occasions, I have encountered patients that have come into A&E straight from the airport,” she claims of her experiences working in emergency medicine. She cautions against practitioners who pressure patients into additional procedures or fail to adequately discuss complications and aftercare. “We are not in the business of making people self-conscious about things that are not a problem for them.”.

Industry observers note that then there’s the phenomenon of “treatment stacking.” While certain procedures can complement one another, squeezing several into a short period of time can increase the likelihood of complications. “Many of these treatments work by creating a controlled injury that the skin then repairs, and doing several close together doesn't give it time to recover,” explains aesthetics doctor Dr. Priya Verma. “That raises the risk of prolonged inflammation, infection and pigmentation changes, particularly in darker skin tones.”.

According to recent reports, multiple procedures can also make it harder to establish which treatment is responsible for an adverse reaction, notes aesthetics doctor Dr. Ahmed El Muntasar. “Ultimately, I’d much rather a patient’s treatment schedule was dictated by how their skin is recovering than by the date of their flight home.”.

Sources indicate that consider, too, how conducive the rest of your vacation itinerary is to your skin’s recovery. As Verma notes, the low humidity in airplane cabins can exacerbate dryness and sensitivity in already compromised skin, while sun exposure can increase the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. There is no universal rule about how soon you can fly after a non-surgical cosmetic procedure, says Khan, but you should allow ample time for recovery and an in-person review before your departure. (With surgical procedures, flying also carries an increased risk of blood clots, making a conversation with your surgeon about your travel looks particularly vital.).

There's also the question of downtime. An unfortunate-looking reflection in the hotel bathroom mirror doesn’t necessarily mean a treatment has been “botched.” Verma makes an notable distinction: “Downtime is the expected redness, swelling or flaking that settles over a few days. Dissatisfaction is when the skin has healed but you're not happy with the result. A complication is a medical problem that needs treating.”.

Knowing what to expect—and for how long—is something to establish with your practitioner well before the treatment itself. The trajectory of your recovery is key: Increasing pain, spreading redness, heat, discharge, or fever warrant prompt medical attention.

Industry observers note that there are, however, symptoms that warrant immediate medical attention. Following dermal filler injections, for example, the FDA advises seeking immediate medical care for unusual pain, changes to your vision, white, gray, or blue discoloration around the injection site, or signs of a stroke. These may indicate that the blood supply has been compromised.

According to recent reports, “If there are red-flag symptoms, don't just get on a plane because you'd rather deal with it at home,” stresses Khan. “Some complications are time-critical, so get seen locally.”.

In non-emergency situations, contact your original practitioner for an in-person review and document your recovery with photographs taken in consistent lighting. El Muntasar recommends obtaining your full treatment records, including the names, quantities, and batch numbers of any injectables, or the device and settings used for laser treatments. Seek an independent medical opinion from someone experienced in managing complications if you remain concerned.

According to recent reports, as distressing as it can be to feel unhappy with your appearance, resist the temptation to immediately book another aesthetic procedure. “Swelling can make certain areas appear overfilled or disproportionate, and adding more filler to try to balance things out can leave a patient with an entirely different problem once that swelling subsides,” explains Banwell.

According to recent reports, “More treatment isn’t always the antidote to treatment,” states Khan. Anti-wrinkle injections can take around two weeks to reach their full effect, filler can take several weeks to settle, and collagen remodeling following laser treatments or microneedling continues for months. The same caution applies to overzealous at-home skincare. “Your freshly lasered face is not the moment to try the acids and retinoids you picked up at duty-free.”.

It has been revealed that and while you might have meticulously mapped out your Seoul shopping itinerary, restaurant reservations, and dermatology appointments, have you given quite as much thought to what happens when you get home? Establishing a plan for follow-up care, obtaining a record of your procedures, and checking whether your insurance covers complications should all factor into the planning process. El Muntasar recommends getting your aftercare plan in writing, including details of who you can contact outside of clinic hours and who is responsible for any additional medical expenses should you need to extend your stay.

It has been revealed that by all means, indulge your K-beauty curiosity. Just make sure you’re approaching your dermatological appointments with a little more discernment than your haul at Olive Young.

Boasting a brief ingredient list and a short cooking time, this easy chicken dish is one you’ll be making all season. Basic butter becomes the star here—it turns brown and nutty, then gets infused with sage and garlic for a savory sauce that’s basted over simply seasoned chicken breasts. A substantial squeeze of lemon, plus its zest, helps balance the richness. This skillet dinner is perfect for a speedy weeknight meal, but it’s also special enough for firm.

Recent findings suggest that the protein:You don’t have to limit yourself to chicken here. Feel free to replace the breasts with pork chops, shrimp, scallops, or skinless salmon or halibut fillets. Simply adjust the cooking time to properly cook the protein, but be sure to maintain a medium heat. While meat and fish are often cooked on medium-high heat for a nice char, it needs to be a bit lower to avoid bitter residue in the pan, since the butter will be browned immediately afterward.

The crunch:The sage leaves crisp while the butter browns, but there are also ways to add more texture. Stirring in a handful of slivered almonds toward the end of cooking adds to the nuttiness of the dish; pine nuts, pistachios, or roughly chopped walnuts would also work. If you have a container of them, feel free to sprinkle some fried onions on top tableside.

Recent findings suggest that storage and serving ideas:This is not a make-ahead situation; it should be eaten immediately after it’s cooked. Serve with a simple salad dressed in a light vinaigrette to balance the richness. To soak up the sauce, mashed potatoes—traditional or sweet—are ideal. Or, to add another nutty element, roast some Brussels sprouts, cauliflower, or butternut squash to eat alongside and round out the meal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you’ve ever scraped a black fleck off a melted spatula into your pasta and wondered what exactly you just ate, congratulations: You’ve already arrived at the case for nontoxic utensils. Swapping out your plastic-handled, mystery-material kitchen tools is one of the easiest upgrades you can make.

Industry observers note that more difficult is choosing a material to commit to. Walk through any kitchen store and you'll encounter wood, silicone, stainless steel, bamboo, and any number of hybrid constructions. Each has its advocates and its limitations. But after thinking through the tradeoffs and cross-referencing what professionals actually reach for day to day, we landed on a clear answer: Silicone is the best material for a nontoxic utensil set, and a five- to six-piece core collection is all most home cooks need to start.

Latest in this update: We added more information about the pros and cons of each of our winning non-toxic utensil sets.

Food-grade silicone is heat-resistant up to around 450°–600°, depending on the manufacturer, which means it’s unlikely to melt against the side of a hot pan or leach chemicals into your food the way that plastic utensils can when exposed to prolonged heat. It's also nonreactive, meaning it won't interact with acidic ingredients like tomato sauce or citrus the way that some metals can. Unlike wood, it's fully dishwasher-safe and nonporous and it won't harbor bacteria or crack over time with repeated washing. And—critically—it won't scratch your enameled cast iron.

Recent findings suggest that there are some things silicone doesn't do especially well. It can feel slightly grippy or drag-heavy compared to a thin fish spatula, for instance, and some silicone utensils pick up odors over time. (The odor issue is real—I've had cheaper silicone spatulas that smelled faintly of dish soap for months.) One other issue you might find is that you can’t scrape a pan very effectively with silicone in a situation where you might want to blend fond into a sauce for flavor (that’s a case for keeping a wooden spoon around). But for the vast majority of everyday cooking tasks—stirring, folding, sautéing, serving—high-quality silicone outperforms the competition on the merits that matter most.

Material: Platinum-cured siliconeSet size: 5 pieces (also available in 3- and 10-piece sets)Heat resistance: Up to 425°FDishwasher safe: Yes.

What we love: GIR (Get It Right) makes some of the best silicone utensils on the market. Its tools are made from 100% platinum silicone, which among other things, is a method that keeps odors off the utensils. It also makes them fully heat-safe and more durable than most other sets. That matters more than it might sound: Many budget silicone utensils use a nylon or fiberglass core to add rigidity, which can become a problem if the silicone outer layer ever cracks or peels. With GIR, what you see is what you get all the way through.

The handles are weighted and ergonomic without being bulky, and the heads are thin enough to actually get under food—like a delicate omelet—which is a genuine problem with thicker silicone spatulas. GIR's tools also hold up unusually well over time. The silicone doesn't discolor, doesn't absorb odors the way cheaper versions can, and doesn't degrade with repeated dishwasher cycles.

Recent findings suggest that the brand offers a range of set configurations, but its core five-piece collection gives you exactly what you need without the extras: a spatula, a flip turner, a spoon, a ladle, and GIR's signature spoonula—a hybrid tool that functions as both spoon and spatula that’s particularly useful for scraping the sides of a pan or transferring food cleanly from pot to bowl. The spoonula in particular gets more use in my kitchen than I expected—it's become the default tool for anything that needs to be scraped, scooped, or transferred.

What we'd leave: It's a bit pricier than other silicone sets, but we think it's well worth it.

Good Grips 3-Piece Silicone Utensil Set.

Material: SiliconeSet size: 3 piecesHeat resistance: Not listed on siteDishwasher safe: Yes.

What we love: Oxo's kitchen tools have been a reliable standard for years, and the brand’s silicone utensil line earns that trust at a lower price point. The set includes a ladle, a cooking spoon, and a turner, with flexible edges designed to get every last bit from pans and bowls. The handles are comfortable and grippy even when wet, and the one-piece silicone construction makes cleanup straightforward.

What we'd leave: It's a leaner starting point than our top pick, but that's not necessarily a bad thing—if you're building a collection piece by piece, this is a smart, low-commitment way to start with utensils you'll actually use.

What we love: Wooden spoons are gentle on cookware, they don't conduct heat, and they have a tactile warmth that silicone can't replicate. The Essentials Set, made by a small wood shop out of Kempton, Pennsylvania, includes a large spatula, a stirring spoon, tongs, a medium serving spoon, a ladle, and Jonathan’s signature Original Spootle—plus a jar of their own SpoonWax to keep everything conditioned.

Material: WoodSet size: Wide range; medium set has 7 piecesHeat resistance: Not listed on siteDishwasher safe: No.

In a recent development, what we'd leave: The wood requires more upkeep (and will eventually crack or warp) compared to silicone, but a quick hand-wash and occasional wipe-down with wax takes about 30 seconds. It's not cheap, but it's a premium product. Just keep it out of the dishwasher. For cooks who prefer the feel of wood, Jonathan's Spoons makes some of the most thoughtfully crafted wooden utensil sets available.

5-Piece Stainless Steel Kitchen Utensil Set.

Material: Stainless steelSet size: 5 piecesHeat resistance: 600°FDishwasher safe: Yes.

What we love: Stainless-steel utensils are indestructible and oven-safe to high temperatures, and they look sharp hanging from a rail or stored in a stylish crock. So why make silicone the top recommendation instead? Bare stainless can scratch nonstick and enameled surfaces, so these are best suited for cooks who primarily use uncoated cookware (carbon steel, stainless steel, cast iron). All-Clad's 5-piece set includes a ladle, a solid spoon, a slotted spoon, a turner, and a storage caddy, all crafted from heavy-gauge stainless steel with ergonomic handles long enough to reach into deep pots. The set is heat-safe up to 600°, dishwasher-safe, and backed by All-Clad's limited lifetime warranty. If you're already cooking on All-Clad stainless-steel pans, this is the obvious companion set.

What we'd leave: If you don't have uncoated cookware, this isn't the set for you.

It has been revealed that once you have your core set, it's worth considering what other tools you'd need. Whether you're pescatarian, a deep-fryer, or an avid wok user, there's a tool out there that'll help you achieve your highest cooking goals. None of these need to come from the same brand—this is where building piece by piece, based on what you actually cook, makes more sense than buying a bigger bundle. Here are a few of our favorites.

Recent findings suggest that if crisping salmon skin is your game, a fish spatula is a must. The Lamson Flexible Stainless-Steel Slotted Turner ($53) is a longtime favorite, but Winco’s Fish Spatula ($10) is an inexpensive alternative with a wooden handle that's still flexible enough for delicate fillets.

Medium Stainless Steel Fish Spatula.

According to recent reports, if steak is more up your alley, you can't be without a pair of tongs. Of course it's great for turning the steak in a skillet and holding in steady while you slice, but this tool is also helpful for a boatload of other tasks, like removing corn cobs from a pot of boiling water and shifting sheet pans around your oven. Oxo’s 12" Locking Tongs ($20) with silicone tips are gentle on nonstick and enameled surfaces while still giving you a confident grip.

It has been revealed that whether you're a deep-fry fanatic or a dumpling enthusiast, a spider strainer is a great tool for removing crisped or boiled items from hot pots and pans. We like this stainless-steel version for its sturdiness and extra-long handle.

Open Kitchen by Williams Sonoma.

A from-scratch dressing, a silky cream sauce, or a fluffy whipped cream is made possible because of a good whisk. You can splurge on the editor-favorite Matfer Bourgeat Piano Whisk or opt for a silicone-coated Oxo Good Grips version.

Recent findings suggest that the same logic that makes a 7-piece cookware set a better starting point than a 15-piece one applies here: More isn't always better, and the average home cook will reach for the same handful of tools repeatedly. A well-considered five-piece silicone set typically covers a large spoon (for stirring sauces, soups, and grains), a slotted spoon (for draining and serving), a flexible spatula (the workhorse for eggs, fish, and pancakes), a turner or solid spatula (for heavier tasks like flipping burgers or moving proteins), and a ladle or tongs, depending on what you cook most.

With five tools, you can execute most stovetop and baking tasks without reaching for anything else. That mentioned, not every set breaks down exactly this way—and that's fine. A three-piece set that covers your everyday tools beats a five-piece set with two pieces you never touch. Think of five as the target, not a hard rule.

Are silicone utensils actually nontoxic?

High-quality, food-grade silicone is considered one of the safest materials for kitchen utensils, with FDA-approved versions specifically tested to ensure they don’t leach harmful substances into food. It's nonreactive, doesn't leach chemicals into food, and is stable at high temperatures. However, the quality of silicone utensils is much more all over the place. Cheaper sets often use filler materials or nylon cores that can degrade over time. Look for utensils made from 100% platinum-cured or pharmaceutical-grade silicone—the kind GIR uses—and you can feel confident about what's touching your food.

How do I take care of my utensils so they last?

It depends on the material. Silicone is the lowest maintenance—most sets are dishwasher-safe and require no special treatment. Wood needs more attention: hand-washing, drying thoroughly after each use, and oiling periodically with food-safe mineral oil or wax. Stainless steel is virtually indestructible, but hand-washing will keep it looking better longer. Regardless of material, avoid soaking utensils for extended periods and store them somewhere with good airflow rather than sealed in a drawer while still damp.

Do I need to match my utensils to my cookware?

Recent findings suggest that not exactly—but it's worth thinking about. If you cook primarily on nonstick or enameled cookware, silicone is your safest bet since it won't scratch delicate surfaces. If you cook mainly on stainless steel or cast iron, you have more flexibility and can use metal utensils without worry. Also, you may need a little more leverage to get food off, and metal can help with that. Wood works well across the board but comes with its own maintenance tradeoffs. The most practical approach for most home cooks: Start with a silicone set as your everyday workhorse, then add a stainless fish spatula or tongs as your cooking demands them.

Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

Industry observers note that in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Sources indicate that combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Sources indicate that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

The Art of Being Veruschka: Fashion Pays Tribute to a Legend

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, “There is and will always be only one Veruschka,” Richard Avedon wrote in the May 1972 glitch of Vogue in an impassioned tribute to his muse. More than half a century later, his words still ring true. Since news broke of the German supermodel’s death at the age of 87, generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models have been reflecting on her immeasurable influence.

A protagonist of some of the most fantastical fashion editorials ever committed to the pages of Vogue and a prolific cover star, Veruschka helped expand the possibilities of what a model could be. Her body was her artistic medium, her imagination as instrumental to the making of a photograph as that of the person behind the lens. Her creative curiosity would endure long after her heyday in the 1960s and ’70s, finding expression in her experiments with body painting and camouflage, her performance art, and her occasional, much-feted returns to the runway.

For those who knew and worked with Veruschka, though, there was as much to marvel at away from the camera: her generosity of spirit, quiet eccentricities, intellectual curiosity, and her sense of humor. In the tributes shared with Vogue below, fellow models recall their first encounters with a woman whose photographs once adorned their bedroom walls, while designers and photographers reflect on the creative communion they shared with her—and how rare a model like Veruschka is today.

It has been revealed that I am so sad to hear the news of Veruschka’s passing. When I started modeling in 1966, she was one of my idols—she was so beautiful and exotic. I had always wanted to meet her, and then in the 1980s, while I was appearing on Broadway in the musical My One and Only, a knock came on my dressing room door after the performance. I opened it and, to my surprise and huge delight, Veruschka was standing there. It was so lovely to finally meet her, and she was absolutely divine, and we chatted for ages. She certainly is one of the greatest of all models. RIP, beautiful lady.

According to recent reports, veruschka was an extraordinary artist that I was blessed to know. Thank you, Vera….

It has been revealed that I remember sitting in the library at Saint Martins, transfixed by the camouflage photographs in Veruschka: Trans-Figurations, the book she made with Holger Trülzsch. Years later, when I had the chance to work with her, I knew I wanted her to close my spring/summer 2011 show. We flew her in from Berlin and made her a bespoke dress for the finale. What I loved about working with her was how open she was to the ideas behind the collection and how wholeheartedly she embraced them. She was 71 and absolutely majestic on the runway. She had a presence unlike anyone else. A creative powerhouse and a true original.

Being a model is an art form, and she was one of the people who truly mastered it. She had both creativity and respect for what she was doing. When we worked with her, she was incredibly impressive. There was an energy, a grace, and a lasting presence that you don’t see so often today. The lifespan of a model’s career seems to have become so much shorter. I sometimes wonder if, in the way the industry works today, we’re leaving less room for someone to become truly iconic.

Sources indicate that when I was a young girl, my bedroom walls were covered in photographs of Veruschka. To me, she looked like she had stepped out of another world—a dream I looked up to, one of the incredible women who had paved the way before me. I used to lie in bed, staring at those pictures, wondering what it would be like actually to know someone like her. Years later, that dream literally knocked on my door.

According to recent reports, we ended up living together at our agent Zoli’s house on East 63rd Street. For months, after a long day’s work, we would settle in for the evening with our sketchbooks. I can still see her drawing her little cats—curled up, stretching out, or peeking from the corners of the pages—while I sketched beside her. We didn’t need to say much; the quiet between us always felt so full.

Veruschka was always an enigma to me, a woman with a poetic soul and a nature I could never quite put a name to. She had a wicked little smile and a twinkle in her eye when she’d look up from her drawing, as if she knew a secret about the world she might someday share. Her voice was low and sensuous, and she was always kinder than anyone needed to be.

Sometimes, while watching her sketch, I would think back to that little girl staring at the pictures on her wall. I wished I could tell her that one day she would be sitting right beside her icon, and that Veruschka would be her friend. I have always loved Veruschka, and I always will. Knowing she taught me that dreams really do come true. She was mine.

Every guy needs the best beard trimmer for his situation. Whether he grows it patchy, keeps it perma-stubbled, or is as lustrous as the A-List beards, a trimmer is mandatory in every beard kit. And not all beard trimmers are alike, which is why the best one for your facial hair style may be different from the next guy’s.

I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices. This list reflects a range of options—some multitaskers, some detailers; some top-shelf, some a better buy for lower budgets. Above all, though, I ask you this: Make sure that the device you choose allows your beard to reach its full potential. That doesn’t mean you need a major bushy beard, but rather, you should be able to achieve whichever style (or a suite of styles) you want to wear over the next few years—which is the minimum amount of time any of these devices should last. Ideally, they’ll hum on for five to 10 years, anyhow.

Sources indicate that here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them. (And while you’re at it, consider my rosters of other grooming tools, from razors and electric shavers, to manscapers and hair clippers.).

In a recent development, no sense in burying the headline: Philips Norelco’s Multigroom 9000 Series is, hands down, the best beard trimmer you can buy. And that’s before factoring in how much more it can do than just keep your facial hair in check than other electric razors that are found in your everyday grooming kit. (It’s also recently been renamed the “All-in-One 9000” but answers to both names.) For the last 5 or 6 years, this has been my single go-to trimmer. Everything else is trying to dethrone it, and so far, no true contest has emerged. In terms of customization and power, this device checks all of the boxes.

It has been revealed that it all starts with the beating heart: "The Multigroom does not compromise on power or battery life, and it's very intuitive to use," claims Fellow Barber’s Head of Education Emily Clark. The battery life truly over-delivers: your mileage may vary since Philips Norelco only claims a (still impressive) six hours of charge, but I got a ridiculous 17 hours of consecutive runtime fresh out of the box, thanks to a lithium ion battery. Speaking of the box, there’s a lot in there, all of it useful. Between the small tooth-like detail attachment and foil shaving head, the Multigroom 9000 makes it easy to style and sculpt with precision. One trimmer even adjusts by tenths of a millimeter to help you get the perfect designer stubble, if that's your aim. And that’s just its beard trimming bona fides. The Multigroom 9000 is also a solid hair trimmer (shout out to that brawny motor and battery again) and body hair trimmer as well. Covering off for three products, and doing it well, suddenly makes the $90 price tag look like a deal.

In a recent development, long-term testing notes: Wouldn’t you know it… I lost the beloved little shaver on this one recently. Heartbreak. (Yeah, I can test a latest one, but I realize now how much of my love for it is pinned on that micro shaving attachment.) I stand by the fact that it’s the best on the market, but without that shaver, the window has opened for me to spend time with other devices, like the Braun below. Let this be a lesson: Don’t unpack your Philips Norelco all-in-one in a hotel room without carefully auditing every single piece when you pack it up again. Adam Hurly.

For this reason, I find it a little less perfect across the board compared to the 9000, but the price-to-precision ratio is hard to match. Long-term testing notes: Recently, I used the 5000 consistently, and got quite cozy with it. Sure, it lacked the key shaving features of the 9000, but I think this is truly the best value device in the game when you only want a trimmer. You want a beard trimmer that’s simple, effective, and doesn’t come with useless features or add-ons. Here are a few features to consider when looking for a great beard trimmer.

Sources indicate that we look at how evenly a trimmer cuts, how comfortable it is to use, and whether its attachments make different jobs easier. Power matters, but so do the small frustrations that become obvious with regular use – awkward combs, difficult cleanup, or a handle that’s hard to hold. We also compare battery life, charging, and the range of cutting lengths against the price.

Adam Hurly has reviewed grooming products since 2013, and his years of testing underpin this guide. Timothy Beck Werth contributes his own hands-on findings alongside his wider coverage of grooming and consumer technology. For this upgrade, we’ve also drawn on my reviews for British GQ, with the relevant tester and any differences between British and US kits identified in the entries. Read more about GQ and how we test and review products.

What is the best beard trimmer?

Sources indicate that there’s no denying: The Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000 is the best beard trimmer you can buy these days. If its $100 price tag is too steep, the baby-brother Multigroom 5000 is a solid fallback. It’s not shower-proof, has a shorter warranty (five years to the 9000’s eight years), has a plastic body instead of steel, and comes with a few less attachments. But at $40, it gets the basics done nearly as well as it’s pricier sibling.

Can you use a beard trimmer to cut head hair?

Sources indicate that beard trimmers are not meant to be used as hair clippers, since clippers require much more power to cut through thicker patches of hair. However, some beard trimmers have the muscle to multitask, and they’ll proudly hype that skill—usually by declaring the work for “beard and head” or similar language. We usually verify those claims against product reviews, too. And frankly, we’d probably just opt to buy a dedicated hair trimmer (you can find our roundup of the best hair trimmers here), especially if you’ll be using it often.

Which beard trimmer do barbers use?

Sources indicate that barbers choose tools to suit the job, from adjustable trimmers for controlling length, to detail trimmers for sharper edges. The Wahl Pro Series High Visibility is our professional pick for precision work, while the Philips Norelco Multigroom range offers broader versatility. For home use, start with your beard length and the kind of maintenance you do most often – a tool built for crisp outlines won’t necessarily include the guards you need to trim a longer beard evenly.

Which trimmer number is best for a beard?

Sources indicate that that's going to depend on what beard style you're going with. In order to play around with trimmer numbers, we like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440 for its easy-to-use adjustment wheel.

How do you use a beard trimmer?

In a recent development, first, wash and dry your beard so you're starting off with a clean canvas. Then, decide how short or long you want to keep that bad boy. Trim against the grain of your growth, and know that the direction of growth may vary even in similar locations on the face. It's OK to make a couple of passes to ensure you get each hair because a patchy beard is a bad beard. Finally, clean up the neckline with some sharp lines so it's neat and tidy, framing the perfection that is your beautiful facial hair.

How do I maintain and clean a beard trimmer?

Switch it off and disconnect the charger before cleaning, then remove trapped hair from the blades and combs after each use. Follow the instructions for your particular model – a washable cutting head doesn’t mean the whole handle can go under the tap. The Remington Vacuum trimmer, for example, has removable washable parts, but its body should stay out of water.

Let washed components dry before putting them away. Oil the blades if the manufacturer tells you to, but don’t assume every trimmer needs it. Philips’ current Multigroom blades are designed to work without oiling. Replace a damaged or persistently blunt cutting unit with the correct part for your model.

How do I choose the right trimmer if I have sensitive skin or ingrown hairs?

Industry observers note that avoid “zero-gap” trimmers, which is a trimmer that cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length—those can mess your skin if you're prone to irritation or ingrowns. Otherwise, since you're trimming, you usually won't have to worry about irritating your skin because the blades shouldn't ever actually make contact with your face.

What’s the best way to travel with a beard trimmer—any TSA or voltage concerns?

Industry observers note that one of the significant concerns for frequent travelers—at least in the USA—is whether they're going to be able to get their beard trimmer through security and not having it buzz during transport. If this is a priority for you, look for a model with a travel lock like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440, which prevents the trimmer from turning on in transit.

How do I clean a waterproof vs. non-waterproof trimmer?

Waterproof trimmers are a breeze: Just hit ‘em with the (usually included) cleaning brush, then wash them off in the sink before drying and applying some oil. Non-waterproof trimmers just skip the rinse, so you’ll have to take extra care with the brush. You can also use spray cleaners specifically designed for grooming electricals depending on your trimmer's care instructions.

What should I do if my trimmer starts pulling hair or losing power?

It has been revealed that first, make sure you've thoroughly cleaned the trimmer. Next, make sure it's fully charged and/or has new batteries. If it's still pulling hair, it's probably time to swap the blades (plenty of companies sell refills on their site, and make sure to check the warranty to see if you qualify for a fresh set). If it's losing power, it might be time to swap the internal battery (check your warranty!) or get a new trimmer altogether. Luckily, we haven't had that glitch with any of the trimmers listed above.

Sources indicate that you’ve been there, excited to join your family for Thanksgiving dinner, only to realize that even the green bean casserole isn’t just veggies. This time, though, you can enjoy the creamiest green bean casserole without the dairy or meat. For the ultimate creamy bite, we make a DIY vegan version of condensed cream of mushroom soup with fresh mushrooms, shallots, and almond milk. We're also super into the onion topping on this casserole—it's broiled in the oven with a touch of oil but so much more fragrant and vibrant in flavor than the fried ones that come in a can.

Recent findings suggest that looking for more vegan Thanksgiving sides? Check out our vegan mashed potatoes! They're loaded with rosemary and garlic. SO. GOOD.

It has been revealed that preheat oven to medium broil and line a medium baking sheet with aluminum foil. In a medium bowl, toss onion with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add flour and Panko and toss until the onions are coated. Broil, tossing every 2 to 3 minutes, until onions are crisp and golden, about 6 to 8 minutes total. Turn oven down to 375°.

Prepare an ice bath. In a large pot of heavily salted boiling water, add green beans and cook until bright green, 3 to 4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon or tongs, rapidly transfer green beans to the ice bath to cool. Drain and transfer to a large bowl.

In a large skillet over medium heat, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil. Add shallots and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until mushrooms are golden, about 5 minutes more. Stir in garlic, then transfer the mixture to the bowl with the green beans.

It has been revealed that heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook until golden, about 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in almond milk and bring to a simmer.

Cook until thickened, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Add the green bean mixture and toss until everything is evenly combined.

Transfer the mixture to a medium casserole dish. Bake until warmed through and bubbling around the edges, about 20 minutes. Top with the "fried" onions and bake for 5 minutes more.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Store leftover green bean casserole in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

In a recent development, I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

In a recent development, mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Sources indicate that set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

It has been revealed that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.
